message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2024) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a copy of the lease and any move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds part of the deposit. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a **safe, sanitary, and livable condition** (e.g., functioning plumbing, heating, electrical, pest control). | • Report problems in writing (email or letter) and give the landlord a reasonable time to fix them. | | **Repair & Maintenance** | • If the landlord fails to repair, you may:
 1. **Pay for the repair** and deduct the cost from your rent (only if the landlord is in default).
 2. **Withhold rent** (after giving notice).
 3. **Sue for damages**. | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease. Late fees are allowed only if the lease states them and they are reasonable. | • Pay on time or negotiate a payment plan if you’re having trouble. | | **Notice Requirements** | • **Month‑to‑month**: 30‑day notice to terminate.
• **Fixed‑term lease**: 30‑day notice before the lease ends.
• **Eviction**: Landlord must give a written notice (usually 3 days for nonpayment, 30 days for lease violations). | • Keep copies of all notices. | | **Privacy & Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Ask for a written notice and keep a record of entries. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, familial status, disability, or source of income (e.g., public assistance). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Security & Safety** | • Landlord must provide working smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors. | • Test detectors regularly; report any issues. | | **Lease Terms** | • The lease must be in writing and signed by both parties. | • Read the lease carefully before signing; ask for clarification on any ambiguous clauses. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • The lease may restrict subletting, but you can negotiate with the landlord. | • Get written permission before subletting. | | **Legal Remedies** | • If the landlord violates your rights, you can:
 1. File a complaint with the Texas Attorney General’s Office.
 2. File a lawsuit in small claims court (up to $20,000).
 3. Seek mediation or arbitration if the lease provides for it. | • Keep all documentation (photos, receipts, correspondence). | --- #### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Security Deposit Limits** – Verify the amount and understand the conditions for its return. 2. **Maintenance Responsibilities** – Clarify who handles repairs and how to report them. 3. **Entry Notice** – Confirm the required notice period for landlord entry. 4. **Late Fees** – Ensure any late fee clause is reasonable and clearly stated. 5. **Discrimination Clauses** – Make sure the lease complies with federal and state anti‑discrimination laws. 6. **Termination Notice** – Know the required notice period for ending the tenancy. --- #### When Things Go Wrong | Issue | First Step | Next Step | |-------|------------|-----------| | Landlord refuses to return deposit | Send a written demand for the deposit plus an itemized statement of deductions. | File a claim in small claims court. | | Unresolved maintenance problem | Submit a written notice to the landlord; give a reasonable deadline. | File a complaint with the Texas Attorney General or HUD; consider withholding rent. | | Unlawful eviction notice | Verify the notice meets legal requirements. | File a lawsuit to stop the eviction; seek temporary housing if necessary. | | Discrimination claim | File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights or HUD. | Pursue legal action if the complaint is denied. | --- #### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division**: [https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov](https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights**: [https://www.tchra.org](https://www.tchra.org) - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)**: [https://www.hud.gov](https://www.hud.gov) - **Texas Small Claims Court**: [https://www.txcourts.gov/small-claims](https://www.txcourts.gov/small-claims) Feel free to ask if you need more specific guidance on a particular situation!
